The identities P2=2A, P4=2A², P6=2A³+3Q²(A+Q) hold for all positive u,v. Strict monotonicity for Q>0 and Q≤A/3 establishes unique inversion and realizability, while fixed A proves lower-order nonidentifiability. Compact inverse estimates and an explicit constant-A quadratic data perturbation prove the sharp half-Hölder threshold. originality.rationale: Direct statement-and-implication comparisons found no established minimal sixth-derivative Fourier-intensity jet or redundancy/stability theorem for three equal-width disjoint intervals. The 2026 full-continuum magnitude result does not imply a finite-jet cutoff; the 2018 complete-distance turnpike construction does not provide the specific moment inverse. A formerly recorded two-interval fourth-jet inverse and a three-interval full-intensity local stability result do not imply this sixth-order equal-width theorem. value.rationale: The 2026 three-interval phase-retrieval obstruction motivates searching for a natural identifiable three-component subclass. The theorem gives a sharp finite-measurement cutoff, explains why the fourth derivative is completely blind, supplies an exact realizability test, and identifies the unique conditioning singularity with optimal exponent. These are natural object/invariant features with direct implications for finite-data Fourier imaging; the fact is not just a renaming of two-interval formulas.
